rejected_commits.reason: Linked (PR #74, 'Make pyyaml safe by default'). It is an ancestor of tag 5.1, so a 'contained in the fixed tag' check accepts it, but it was reverted by ccc40f3e2ba384858c0d32263ac3e3a6626ab15e before 5.1 shipped (4.1 was retracted). Its changes are not in the 5.1 code.

truth_evidence: Affected: every release before 5.1 (last vulnerable tag 3.13; tag 4.1 is retracted). Fixed in 5.1.

Fix commit 0cedb2a ('Deprecate/warn usage of yaml.load(input)', lib/ = Python 2 copy) and its Python 3 counterpart 857dff1 ('Apply FullLoader/UnsafeLoader changes to lib3'). Both are in tag 5.1 and not in 3.13. https://github.com/yaml/pyyaml/commit/0cedb2a0697b2bc49e4f3841b8d4590b6b15657e

yaml.load and yaml.load_all change from 'def load(stream, Loader=Loader)' to 'Loader=None' with a warning and FullLoader as the default: the vulnerable behaviour was the unsafe default Loader (lib3/yaml/__init__.py).

Constructor.find_python_module, find_python_name and make_python_instance gain an 'unsafe' parameter and refuse imports / arbitrary classes when it is false; the class is renamed FullConstructor in the fix (lib3/yaml/constructor.py). They are named by their pre-fix class, Constructor.

Module level: the add_constructor/add_multi_constructor registrations in yaml/constructor.py move from Constructor to FullConstructor, with python/object/apply and friends later split off to UnsafeConstructor.
Cosmetic: safe_load and safe_load_all are touched by 857dff1 but only their docstrings change; they are not vulnerable.
Added, not vulnerable: full_load, full_load_all, unsafe_load, unsafe_load_all, warnings, load_warning, FullLoader, UnsafeLoader, CFullLoader, CUnsafeLoader.
Entry points are the two public functions themselves; nothing else in the package calls them.
notes: The explicitly unsafe names (yaml.Loader, yaml.CLoader, yaml.UnsafeLoader) are not listed as entry points: using them is the documented unsafe behaviour, not this advisory.
The two-commit fix (one per lib/ and lib3/ copy) must merge into one set of names.
